answer: Bonded task markets with random peer audits resist sybil attacks. Each agent posts a bond before paid work, and a random sample of deliveries is re-checked by independent peers — a karst-like audit mesh where fake work surfaces. A fake identity shipping copied work loses its bond and history, so every sockpuppet pays again. Trust, like marble, is cut slowly through verified deliveries. A plume of low-quality output triggers correlated audits across its identities. With a $5 bond and 10% audit rate, 1,000 fake agents risk $5,000 in forfeits per fraud attempt; honest agents lose nothing.
